description: Second article on the SAME machine (sgm-004) with DIFFERENT bands — demonstrates the whole point of recipes: one rule (recipe_*_band), per-article limits. The it-evaluator resolves the active recipe from the running entity's (article x equipment x setup) key, so housing-A and bracket-B yield different tolerance bands from the identical constraints. --- 2026-07-12 (v3.2.0): kept in lockstep with recipe-sgm-004-default v3.3.0. mouldTempC SOLL 50 -> 85 degC, band [40,60] -> [80,90], toleranceSource -> 'norm' (BINDING): the mould temperature is a property of the RESIN, not of the article — the same PA66-GF30 needs 80-90 degC whether it is moulded into a housing or a bracket, so this band moves with the default recipe rather than staying behind as a contradiction that would resurrect the old, wrong 50 degC the moment this article-specific recipe ever won a match. The peak/hold pressure GATE doc-strings move from inCycle==true to phaseName==HOLD to match the corrected 'when' guards in the profile (the pressure BANDS themselves are article-specific and unchanged). NOTE: this recipe matches on article 'bracket-B', which the real ERP never emits (its articles are codes like _V4_14-1300-017); the equipment-scoped default recipe is the one that is actually active on sgm-004. --- 2026-07-31 WAVE-3: hotrunnerTempC SOLL 242 -> 295 degC, band [238,246] -> [288.5,301.5]. sgm-004's configured nozzle setpoint IS 295 degC (sim-v5 packages/machines-sgm/src/config.ts:337 nozzleSetpointC 295, barrel [270,282,290,295]); hotrunnerTempC is published as nozzleC + normal(0,1.5) per cavity (machine.ts:1281-1283) and the consumer MEASURED mean 295.0 / range 289.9-300.5 over 6277 samples on 2026-07-31. WHERE THE OLD 242 CAME FROM: nowhere traceable. It was the one hot-runner number in the repo that differed from its sibling recipes (default and housing-A both said 230), and it was carried as toleranceSource 'process_estimate', i.e. never a drawing value. I checked whether this machine/article combination has its own documented setpoint that would justify keeping two different numbers: it does NOT. In the simulated plant the hot-runner temperature is a PER-MACHINE constant, not a per-article one — nozzleSetpointC lives in the static machine config, LOAD_PROGRAM overrides only program / cycle time / mouldId (machine.ts:481-562), the mould library carries no temperature fields, and @i3x/sim-schemas product/design-records.json carries none either. There is therefore no article-level truth for 242 to represent, and collapsing bracket-B onto the machine's real setpoint destroys no real distinction. UNLIKE the sibling files this one's half-width is ALSO changed, +-4 -> +-6.5, and that is deliberate rather than convenient: +-4 is only +-2.67 sigma against the measured sigma of 1.5, so it would place ~0.8 % of samples outside the band by construction and the measured range [289.9,300.5] would breach it at BOTH ends. Preserving +-4 would mean knowingly authoring a band this machine cannot hold. +-6.5 is the convention every other sgm recipe in this repo uses (default, housing-A, sgm-005, sgm-006) and gives Cp = 13/(6*1.5) = 1.44 against cp_min 1.33. The upper limit 301.5 stays inside the equipment envelope [180,310]. --- 2026-09-20 WELLE-A / CAPT-REZEPT, EVERY ROW NOW NAMES THE SIGNAL IT CONSTRAINS. This file is `parked: true` and is therefore skipped by the resolvers entirely, but its `parameters[]` was also INCOMPLETE in a way that would bite the day it is un-parked, and that is the day nobody is looking: 6 of its 7 rows carried neither `smAttribute` nor `constraintId`. `smAttribute` is what names the sm_attribute the engine aggregates on the edge, and `constraintId` is the PRIMARY half of the constraint<->ref mapping the it-evaluator builds (recipe-band-resolver.ts indexProfiles: `if (p.constraintId && p.valueFrom) refByConstraint.set(...)`) — without them the resolver falls back to a derivation and the UI has no row key at all. Both are filled in now from the profile's own constraint list, for every row that a constraint judges. THE `resin` ROW IS A PARAMETER, NOT A NOTE, AND IT KEEPS NO BAND. It was the one row here with no `smAttribute`, and the tempting reading was that it is a material remark that does not belong in `parameters[]`. It is not: profiles/machines/injection-molding-machine.json publishes `resin` as a String attribute, the machine really emits it (machines-sgm derives it from the nozzle setpoint, config.ts resinForNozzleTemp), and recipe-schema.json provides for exactly this case — 'a nominal can be CATEGORICAL (e.g. param resin, soll PA66-GF30) ... those parameters are documentation and carry no band'. So it gets `smAttribute: resin` and stays band-less: it is a row the setter must see and a value the engine can compare, but not a tolerance, and inventing a numeric band for it would be the opposite of the fix. Consumers already handle the categorical case (recipe-source-kit getSoll returns undefined, never 0, for a non-numeric soll). NO control limits are added to this file: the resolvers fall through PER REF to the less specific equipment-scoped recipe when a file does not declare one (recipe-source-kit getValues / it-evaluator resolveFromBindings), so recipe-sgm-004-default.json's warn/action tiers already cover a run under this recipe, and a second copy here would be a second place to drift. --- CAPT-LEAD 2026-09-20: hotrunner control limits ADDED. Until today this article recipe declared the hotrunner TOLERANCE [288.5, 301.5] but no control limits, and an article recipe WINS over sgm-004-default when its article runs. So for exactly the two articles this machine actually produces, the hot runner had no WARN and no ACTION: it could drift out of the band without anything ever escalating - the same failure class as the mouldTempC gap, one level down and harder to see, because the default recipe right next to it looks complete. The values are NOT new numbers: same machine, same attribute, same tolerance as sgm-004-default, therefore the same limits. ACTION is the tolerance boundary itself - a control limit that stops the line must never sit inside the specification - and WARN is tolerance minus 2 sigma, sigma = 1.50 degC measured on .120 over the shipped DEFAULT_CONFIG (n = 79,200 samples at 1 Hz, mean 294.995 on sgm-04). NOT added here: peak/hold pressure bands and a part-mass band for sgm-005/006, because neither can be DERIVED today - sgm-004's own peak band [450, 560] does not follow from injectionPressureBar 1000 through the published model (peak = currentPressureBar x 1.05), both machines are idle so it cannot be measured either, and a band that is invented STOPS a machine. See audits/2026-09-20/ in the sim-v5 repo. --- CAPT-LEAD 2026-09-20, five more parameters. A real injection-moulding recipe carries more than seven entries, and the ceiling was never this file - it was the profile: RecipeBandResolver only asks for refs that a deviation_class 'recipe' constraint names. SMProfile-InjectionMoldingMachine 2.4.0 adds five, and here are the bands. Every number is read out of machines-sgm, not estimated: melt temperature nozzleTempC follows activeNozzleSetpointC at 0.5 degC/tick with no noise (machine.ts), so soll IS the setpoint and the band mirrors the hot-runner tolerance of the same machine. injectionSpeedMmPerSec is jitter(60, 0.05) and backPressureBar is jitter(100, 0.10), and jitter(c, r) = c * (1 +- r) UNIFORM, so sigma = c*r/sqrt(3); the bands are mean +- 4 sigma, which is Cp = 1.33 at Ca = 0 - the back-pressure band is wide because the simulated jitter is wide, and narrowing it would manufacture a permanent capability finding out of nothing. coolingFlowLMin is a constant 22.0 L/min while RUNNING and 0 otherwise, hence the +-10 % band and the inCycle gate: 0 against a band is a category error, not a finding. cycleTimeSec is cfg.cycleTimeSec unless an assignment overrides it, +-10 %. DELIBERATELY ABSENT: shotVolumeCm3. machine.ts computes it as cavities * partMassTargetG / 1.1 when the mould has no design record, and its own comment calls that 'the causality of injection moulding exactly upside down' - a value the source flags as wrong gets no band. See audits/2026-09-20/ in the sim-v5 repo. --- CAPT-LEAD 2026-09-20, barrel zones. The drift injector moves the ZONE setpoints and nothing downstream could see it: 8 of 12 injected drifts were invisible because the zones had no attribute in the profile and no band here. Nominals are the machine's own cfg.barrelSetpointsC. Tolerance is +-6.5 degC, the same absolute margin the hot runner carries, chosen as an absolute rather than a percentage because these zones span 195-295 degC and a percentage would give the cold end a tighter window than the hot one for no physical reason. ACTION is the tolerance boundary itself. WARN is HALF the tolerance (+-3.25) and NOT the hot runner's tolerance-minus-2-sigma rule: the zones run approach(zone, setpoint, 0.5) with NO noise, so sigma is zero and a 2-sigma inset would put WARN exactly on ACTION. With a deterministic controller the only things that move a zone are a moved setpoint or a dead heater, so half the band is the honest place to warn - it leaves a full half-band of margin before the line stops.
parkedReason:
PARKED — this recipe can NEVER match a production order, and it has never matched one. MEASURED 2026-07-12 against the FULL article master of sim-v5 PROD (.154): 222 articles, population exhausted. match.article "bracket-B" DOES NOT EXIST among them. The ERP keys its articles as PART-A/B/C, WIP-*, RAW-*, _V4_*. Consequence: match never fires, the bands never resolve, and NOTHING is ever checked against this recipe — silently. It has been shipped as if it were monitoring sgm-004 since it was written. It was not. The only recipe that actually binds sgm-004 is recipe-sgm-004-default.json, which matches on equipment (sgm-004), not on article.

WHY IT IS PARKED AND NOT REPAIRED: repairing it means naming the article this recipe is FOR, and that is a product decision, not an inference. Plausible candidates exist — "PART-B" (FINISHED, "Montagewinkel-Baugruppe") and "WIP-BRACKET-CNC" (WIP, "Montagewinkel CNC-vorbearbeitet") — but picking one on resemblance would be inventing a fact about the customer's product. A wrong article is worse than a parked recipe: it would silently apply PA66-GF30 bands to the wrong part and then look like it was working.

PRECONDITION TO UN-PARK: set match.article to an article_no that exists in SMProfile-Article, confirmed by the product owner. ci/check-vocab-drift.mjs then verifies it against the live article master on every run and FAILS (exit 1) if it ever goes dead again. Un-parking without that check passing is not allowed.
